title: Sequences, Series and Sigma Notation
seo_title: Precalculus Sequences, Series and Sigma Notation Worksheets (TEKS P.5A–P.5E)
standard_text: P.5A evaluate finite sums and geometric series, when possible, written in sigma notation; P.5B represent arithmetic sequences and geometric sequences using recursive formulas; P.5C calculate the nth term and the nth partial sum of an arithmetic series in mathematical and real-world problems; P.5D represent arithmetic series and geometric series using sigma notation; P.5E calculate the nth term of a geometric series, the nth partial sum of a geometric series, and sum of an infinite geometric series when it exists
meta_desc: Free Precalculus worksheets on sequences and series for Texas TEKS P.5A to P.5E: sigma notation, arithmetic and geometric series, infinite series and recursive formulas. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Arithmetic adds d; geometric multiplies by r.
key_sub: Infinite geometric sum a₁ ÷ (1 − r) only when |r| < 1.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Arithmetic: add d each time; an = a1 + (n − 1)d; Sn = n2(a1 + an).
  • Geometric: multiply by r; an = a1rn−1; Sn = a11 − rn1 − r.
  • Infinite geometric series: if |r| < 1, S = a11 − r; otherwise there is no sum.
  • Recursive formula: give the first term and the rule from one term to the next.

Examples

Example

3 + 6 + 12 + … (8 terms)

a1 = 3, r = 2

S8 = 3(1 − 256) ÷ (1 − 2)

Answer: 765

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
n instead of n − 1an = a1 + (n − 1)d.
Adding the ratioGeometric terms are multiplied by r.
An infinite sum with |r| ≥ 1No sum: the terms do not shrink.

faq.q: What is the difference between a sequence and a series?
faq.a: A sequence is a list; a series is the sum of its terms.
